key_insight: S-Agent shows that spatial reasoning improves when an AI system can use tools to gather and accumulate evidence across views and time, instead of making a one-shot guess from a single image. The key breakthrough is turning spatial understanding into an active, evidence-building process over continuous 3D scenes.
problem_solved: Existing vision-language models and tool-augmented agents are mostly stateless and rely on isolated visual observations, which limits their ability to reason about real-world 3D environments that change over time. This paper addresses the gap between static image understanding and continuous spatial intelligence.
method: Introduces S-Agent, a spatial tool-use agentic paradigm for multi-view images and videos.
Reframes spatial reasoning as spatio-temporal evidence accumulation rather than frame-level prediction.
Uses tool interactions to progressively collect, organize, and reason over observations from a changing 3D world.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more reliable way to build agents for robotics, embodied AI, navigation, and video understanding. It points toward systems that can reason like humans do in real spaces: by exploring, verifying, and accumulating evidence over time.
visual_elements: A before-vs-after diagram comparing static single-frame inference with S-Agent's multi-step evidence accumulation.
A 3D scene timeline showing how observations from multiple views are combined over time.
An agent workflow graphic with tool icons for viewing, querying, tracking, and reasoning.
A loop/stack illustration showing spatio-temporal evidence being gathered and refined.
paper_title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
paper_authors: Yalun Dai, Hao Li, Shulin Tian, Runmao Yao, Yuhao Dong
